hypothesis: Checkpoint inspection reduces agent-visible startup bytes by at least 10 percent on a verified clean fresh clone while preserving the permitted-task decision and exposing any declared stale evidence.
limitations: One sequential self-use task on a detached clean fresh clone. The checkpoint added 617 agent-visible bytes and hashed 118285 declared-evidence bytes plus a 6650-byte checkpoint, but internal filesystem bytes are reported separately rather than treated as model context. No incremental setup was needed and no operational report or maintenance cost was omitted; policy-required evaluation logging and existing implementation maintenance are excluded, which can only make the failed intervention look more favorable. The result does not cover dirty or long-lived worktrees, latency, semantic dependency completeness, or downstream task success.
